item.title: Kumamoto Tea Country — Guide
item.description: The highlands of the Aso region and Kumamoto’s mountains are dotted with beautiful green-tea plantations, where neat rows of tea bushes carpet the rolling hills in vivid green. Kumamoto produces well-regarded Japanese green tea, and its cool, misty upland climate and volcanic soils are ideal for cultivating it. In tea-growing villages, visitors can take in the scenic terraced fields, especially lovely in the fresh green of the new-leaf season in late spring, learn about tea cultivation and processing, and — depending on the spot — sample or buy fresh local tea, enjoy tea-flavoured sweets, or join seasonal tea-picking experiences.

item.title: Yamato Tea: Nara's Highland Green Tea — Guide
item.description: Yamato-cha is the green tea of Nara, grown for centuries on the cool, mist-wrapped highlands of the prefecture’s east around Tsukigase, Yamazoe and the Yamato plateau. The region’s elevation, temperature swings and morning fogs create ideal conditions for tea of fine aroma and mellow depth, and though less famous than Uji or Shizuoka, Yamato-cha is a quietly excellent tea prized by connoisseurs, produced as sencha, kabusecha and hojicha. Neatly terraced plantations climb the highland slopes, some farms welcome visitors for tastings, and the tea makes a natural pairing with Nara’s wagashi and a refined local souvenir.

item.title: Uji Matcha & Tea Culture Guide: Kyoto's Green Gold
item.description: Matcha — the vivid green, stone-ground powdered tea whisked into a frothy bowl — is inseparable from Kyoto, and its finest expression comes from Uji, a small city on Kyoto’s southern edge that has been Japan’s most prestigious tea-growing region for some 800 years. Uji matcha is the green gold of Japanese tea: the powder behind the tea ceremony, and the flavour behind an endless parade of Kyoto sweets, from soft-serve to parfaits to delicate wagashi.
